IN MY OPINION, the questions were not 100% clear and could have been written differently. For instance, if the scenario says they DID NOT eat something and I am asked how much they liked it makes no sense to me.
Still on the scenarios, I really don't think they're clear or realistic to analyze. For instance, two people that are not relatively intimate or close to each other would NEVER lick from the same ice cream cone. There's nothing to evaluate there. They would simply NOT do it.
Anyway, I tried to be as honest as possible here, but I really don't like my own answers for multiple of the questions.

This whole thing seemed rather pointless to me as I literally could have answered anything for any scenario. The data provided offered almost no insight as to what they liked, save a few times and I am not a mind reader for the rest. I could literally have just chosen moderate for every answer except a couple. I only slightly strayed from that to mix it up some. I am thinking perhaps better instructions and clearer scenarios with more data might help more accurate data, though I do not really know the point. I just know that I could close my eyes and guess and my answers could be just as correct.

This was really hard to wrap my head around, especially the choice before the actions. The instructions said, "By how much the two people would like the food, we mean how much eating it would satisfy the motivational state they are in right now — for example, how hungry they are, or how much they like or are interested in that kind of food. This is about the appeal of the food itself, separate from what they decide to do and from how easy or hard it is to get or eat the food." Well, if we don't know about each person's preference, how can we determine how much they like the food with no background information? Just seems flawed to me.
